correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge4\), the polar equals the zero-sum cube section \(H_n\cap[-1,1]^n\). Exact polar vertex and edge classifications give the full ridge census. Facet-normal dot products yield one parity-dependent exterior dihedral angle. Each ridge is a simplex on \(N=n-2\) signed projected-coordinate vectors with Gram matrix \(G=I_N-ss^{\mathsf T}/n\); its determinant is \(2/n\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}G^{-1}\mathbf1=N+(\sum_i s_i)^2/2\). This analytically determines all ridge measures. The classical polyhedral external-angle face formula gives \(V_{n-3}\), and Stirling and arccosine expansions prove the parity-neutral limit. The standalone check.py independently enumerates every edge, simplex volume, and facet-normal angle for \(4\le n\le8\), but finite experiments are not used as a proof for all orders. At \(n=4\) the known cube invariant \(V_1=3\) is recovered.

value.rationale: The second Steiner coefficient is a canonical metric curvature invariant and a motivated missing complement to the known volume/combinatorial theory of the Van Kampen–Flores family. A single exact ridge isometry class across all high dimensions is structural, not a simple renaming or arbitrary slice. Full all-dimensional curvature, including an explicit asymptotic parity cancellation between face counts and dihedral angles, informs the geometric comparison of different parity realizations. The limit does not claim an unrelated downstream theorem.
